newsitem.title: LEBANON: Troops out in Beirut as general strike begins.
newsitem.headline: Troops out in Beirut as general strike begins.

text.p: Troops were in the streets of Beirut on Thursday as most shops and schools closed in response to a general strike call by opponents of Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri.

A broad spectrum of opposition groups backed by labour unions, students and media workers called the one-day strike in protest at Hariri's media policies, his perceived lack of social policies and a standing ban on public demonstrations.
The strike organisers have called a demonstration in Beirut at 11 a.m. (0900 GMT) but the government has said it is banned and that the army and security forces are responsible for maintaining order.
Troops manned checkpoints across Beirut, stopping traffic and checking identities. Foot patrols of soldiers in full battledress toured the streets.
Troops also sealed off the area around the prime minister's offices in west Beirut and the area where the demonstration was due to take place.
